title: Registry Vendor Fraud Detection - Red Flags and Verification Protocol
content:
REGISTRY VENDOR FRAUD DETECTION PROTOCOL

Purpose: Standardized checklist for evaluating registry service vendors to avoid fraudulent offers, data compromise, and financial loss.

BACKGROUND:
Investigative journalists are increasingly targeted by fraudulent registry service vendors exploiting:
• Professional urgency (investigation deadlines)
• Budget constraints (appeal of extreme discounts)
• Limited vendor knowledge (offshore jurisdictions)
• Trust in "journalist-exclusive" offers

RED FLAGS - PROMOTIONAL OFFERS:
🚩 Unsolicited emails with "exclusive journalist pricing"
🚩 Extreme discounts (>40%) significantly above industry norms (15-20%)
🚩 Artificial urgency (24-48 hour deadlines, "limited inventory")
🚩 Vague or unverifiable "original prices"
🚩 "Unlimited" query promises (no legitimate vendor offers truly unlimited)
🚩 Pressure tactics ("first-come, first-served", "API rate limits", "only X slots available")
🚩 Generic email domains (Gmail, ProtonMail) for business communications
🚩 Recently registered companies (<6 months) with no track record
🚩 No published refund or data retention policies
🚩 Timing coincides with active investigations (suggests data broker intelligence)

VERIFICATION PROTOCOL:

1. COMPANY LEGITIMACY CHECK
   □ Verify company registration (Companies House, state registries)
   □ Check domain registration age (WHOIS lookup)
   □ Search for journalist testimonials or case studies
   □ Cross-reference with IJN vetted vendor directory
   □ Verify physical address (not just PO box or virtual office)

2. PRICING VERIFICATION
   □ Compare against industry benchmarks (IJN surveys, peer networks)
   □ Request pricing verification from established competitors
   □ Calculate effective per-query rate (if "unlimited" claimed)
   □ Assess whether discount percentage is realistic (15-20% typical)
   □ Verify "original price" through independent sources

3. TECHNICAL CAPABILITY ASSESSMENT
   □ Confirm direct registry access (not reselling others' data)
   □ Verify turnaround time claims with trial queries
   □ Check document certification standards
   □ Assess data security and retention policies
   □ Request references from other journalists

4. RISK ANALYSIS
   □ Evaluate opportunity cost vs established vendors
   □ Assess impact of non-delivery on investigation timeline
   □ Consider data compromise risk (source protection)
   □ Review refund policy for non-performance
   □ Calculate sunk cost if vendor fails to deliver

INDUSTRY PRICING BENCHMARKS (Q1 2026):
• Panama corporate registry: €22-€28/query (24hr turnaround)
• Cayman Islands: €25-€32/query
• Cyprus: €8-€12/query
• BVI: €30-€38/query
• Jersey: €15-€20/query
• Bulk discounts: 15-20% for 100+ queries
• Multi-jurisdiction bundles: €300-€600 for 3-4 jurisdictions
• Expedited service: +€10-€15/query for 6hr turnaround

VETTED VENDORS (IJN Directory, Feb 2026):
✓ Global Registry Direct (GRD)
✓ European Corporate Intelligence (ECI)
✓ Transparency International Registry Services
✓ OpenCorporates Pro
✓ Corporate Watch International

DECISION FRAMEWORK:

ACCEPT if:
• Vendor in IJN vetted directory OR
• 2+ journalist references verifiable AND
• Pricing within industry benchmark range (±25%) AND
• Company registration >12 months AND
• Clear refund/data retention policies AND
• No artificial urgency or pressure tactics

REJECT if:
• Extreme discount (>40%) with no verifiable justification OR
• Artificial urgency (<72 hour deadline) OR
• Unsolicited offer timed to active investigation OR
• No verifiable journalist references OR
• Pricing >50% below industry benchmarks OR
• Generic email domain for business communications OR
• No published refund policy

DEFER if:
• Pricing competitive but vendor unknown (request trial query) OR
• Mixed signals (some red flags, some legitimate indicators) OR
• Time permits thorough due diligence (>1 week available)

CASE STUDY - REGISTRY INTELLIGENCE (FEB 2026):
Received: Feb 14, 2026
Offer: 60% discount (€899 → €359.60) Panama/Cayman bundle, 48hr deadline
Red flags identified: 8/10 fraud indicators
Verification: Company 4 months old, no journalist references, pricing 72-87% below market
Decision: REJECT - forwarded to IJN security team
Outcome: Preserved €265 budget for verified GRD premium queries

REPORTING:
Suspicious offers should be reported to:
• IJN Security Team: security@investigativejournalists.org
• Include: promotional email, company details, red flags identified
• Helps protect broader journalist community

REVIEW CYCLE:
Update benchmarks quarterly based on:
• IJN vendor surveys
• Peer network pricing intelligence
• Personal vendor experience
• Industry rate changes

Last updated: February 14, 2026
Next review: May 1, 2026

title: Investigative Newsletter Triage Protocol - Signal vs Noise Classification
content:
# Investigative Newsletter Triage Protocol

## Purpose
Standardized protocol for filtering and categorizing subscription emails from investigative journalism organizations, registry research tools, and financial crime reporting networks. Distinguishes high-value professional development content from promotional vendor noise.

## Newsletter Source Classification

### Tier 1: High-Signal Professional Organizations
- **ICIJ (International Consortium of Investigative Journalists)**: Infrastructure updates, access protocol changes, methodology resources
- **OCCRP (Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project)**: Security alerts, verification tools, source protection updates
- **Investigative Journalism Network**: Cross-border collaboration opportunities, training programs

**Triage Priority**: Immediate review for investigation-critical intelligence

### Tier 2: Registry Vendor Communications
- **European Corporate Intelligence (ECI)**: Service updates, jurisdictional coverage changes
- **Global Registry Direct (GRD)**: Platform feature releases, pricing changes
- **Registry Intelligence**: Competitor landscape intelligence

**Triage Priority**: Extract vendor landscape intelligence, flag promotional upsells

## Content Classification Framework

### CLEARVIEW-Critical (Immediate Action Required)
- New registry access protocols affecting active investigation jurisdictions
- Vendor fraud alerts impacting document verification standards
- Security incidents requiring source protection protocol updates
- Jurisdictional database launches enabling cost savings

### General Methodology (Background Reading)
- Interview technique workshops
- Cross-border investigation case studies
- Source protection best practices
- Data analysis training programs

### Vendor Landscape Intelligence (Procurement Context)
- Pricing changes from existing vendors
- New competitor service launches
- Feature comparison data
- Market consolidation news

## Promotional Content Red Flags
- "Limited time offer" urgency language
- Discount expiration deadlines
- "Educational webinar" disguising sales pitch
- Pricing presented before methodology value
- Upgrade pressure tied to trial expiration

## Consolidation Output Format

### Structured Digest Template
```
## CLEARVIEW-Critical Intelligence
[Immediate action items with timeline impact]

## General Methodology Updates  
[Professional development content for future reference]

## Vendor Landscape Intelligence
[Pricing changes, new competitors, service updates]

## Promotional Noise (Flagged for Deletion)
[Vendor upsell attempts with no intelligence value]
```

## Cross-Reference Requirements
- Vendor service announcements → Existing CLEARVIEW vendor relationships (finance records)
- Registry protocol updates → Active investigation jurisdictions (calendar, todo)
- Pricing changes → Budget constraints (finance caps)
- Security alerts → Source communication protocols (contacts, encrypted channels)

## Review Cadence
- Weekly triage: Every Monday morning
- Ad-hoc triage: When investigation-critical keywords detected (Panama, Cyprus, beneficial ownership, fraud alert)

---
Last Updated: 2026-03-30
Owner: Priya Iyer, Financial Crime Desk

title: Source Interview Platform Selection - Legal Compliance Requirements (Post-2024 Settlement)
content:
# Source Interview Platform Selection - Legal Compliance Requirements

## Background: Blackstone v. Morning Ledger Settlement (2024)

In 2024, Morning Ledger settled a defamation lawsuit (Blackstone Capital Partners v. The Morning Ledger) for $340,000. The case exposed three confidential sources due to discoverable server logs from a third-party video conferencing platform used for source interviews. The settlement agreement includes binding protocols for future source communications.

## Hard Legal Constraints (Non-Negotiable)

All platforms used for confidential source interviews must satisfy:

1. **End-to-end encryption with no server-side decryption capability**
   - Platform provider must not have technical ability to decrypt communications
   - No "lawful intercept" backdoors or key escrow

2. **No persistent server-side artifacts**
   - No server-side recording capabilities
   - No persistent logs of participant metadata (IP addresses, connection times, device identifiers)
   - RAM-only logging acceptable if wiped on session termination

3. **Jurisdiction outside EU/UK discovery frameworks**
   - Avoid platforms hosted in jurisdictions with broad discovery/disclosure obligations
   - Preferred: US jurisdiction (First Amendment protections) or Swiss jurisdiction (strong privacy laws)
   - Alternative: Self-hosted infrastructure under Morning Ledger's direct control

4. **Documented source-protection certification**
   - Platform must have published security audit or source-protection certification
   - Acceptable certifications: EFF Secure Messaging Scorecard, ACLU journalist-protection endorsement

## Compliant Platform Options

### Tier 1: Recommended
- **Signal** (group video calls): E2EE, ephemeral, US jurisdiction, EFF-certified
- **Wire** (conference calls): E2EE, Swiss jurisdiction, enterprise source-protection tier

### Tier 2: Acceptable with Configuration
- **Self-hosted Jitsi**: Requires custom configuration (recording disabled, RAM-only logs, VPN-only access)
- **Self-hosted BigBlueButton**: Similar requirements to Jitsi

### Non-Compliant Platforms (DO NOT USE)
- **Zoom** (server-side decryption capability, US jurisdiction but broad discovery exposure)
- **Google Meet** (server-side decryption, extensive metadata logging)
- **Microsoft Teams** (server-side decryption, enterprise compliance features create discovery risk)
- **Third-party hosted Jitsi** (server-side recording, EU jurisdiction if hosted by European partners)
- **Skype** (Microsoft-owned, same issues as Teams)

## Workflow Implications

Compliant platforms may lack features common in non-compliant alternatives:
- No built-in transcription (requires manual note-taking)
- No collaborative document editing (use separate encrypted tools)
- May require participant software installation

These workflow trade-offs are acceptable. Source protection is the non-negotiable priority.

## Approval Process

Any platform not listed in Tier 1/2 above requires explicit written approval from General Counsel (Rajesh Mehta) before use with confidential sources.

## References
- Settlement Agreement: Blackstone Capital Partners v. The Morning Ledger (SDNY 2024-CV-8472)
- EFF Secure Messaging Scorecard: https://www.eff.org/secure-messaging-scorecard
- Morning Ledger Source Protection Policy (updated 2024-09-15)

---
Last updated: 2026-03-29
Document owner: Rajesh Mehta, General Counsel
Review cycle: Annual (next review: 2027-03-29)
